transcript.text: My indesit washing machine fills with water and drains but the drum just doesn't go round at all. Its an IWC something. Had it about 9 years. Is it worth fixing?

To answer your question first: for a 9-year-old Indesit, if this is just a belt or carbon brushes (which are common wear parts), it is usually worth fixing as the repair cost is low. If it's the motor itself or bearings, it might be nearing the end of its life. The most likely cause on an Indesit of this age is that the rubber drive belt has slipped off or snapped. Another possibility is that the carbon brushes in the motor are worn out (they wear down over time like brake pads). 1. Take all the washing out of the machine.
2. Select a 'Spin Only' programme and start it.
3. Watch what happens: does the drum spin up to speed normally when empty? Please let me know if it spins properly with nothing in it, or if it still just sits there.

I tried Spin Only with the drum empty and it still just sits there. The drum doesn't turn at all, and I can't hear the motor running. I should mention that a few weeks ago I noticed a faint hot electrical smell, but I haven't noticed it since. What should I check next?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. The faint hot electrical smell you noticed a few weeks ago is the key clue here. On Indesit machines of this age, that smell usually means the carbon brushes in the motor have worn down enough to spark inside the motor casing. This heat can blow the motor's internal thermal fuse (a safety cut-out) or damage the windings. Because you now have a confirmed electrical burning hazard and the drum will not turn at all, this is no longer an owner-safe check situation. The machine must be isolated from the mains immediately. Do not attempt to run it again or try to force the drum by hand while it is plugged in. You need to call a qualified appliance engineer to check the motor (and likely the carbon brushes and thermal fuse). Given the age of the machine, ask the engineer for a quote; if the repair cost is high, it may be worth considering replacement, but often a motor/brush replacement on an Indesit is reasonably priced compared to buying new. Please unplug the machine now and arrange for an engineer visit.
